01 / why not the official registry

The official registry lists everything. This one has an opinion.

◆

Curated, not exhaustive

Every entry meets written inclusion criteria: active upstream maintenance and real users. Stale entries get removed, not archived.

CRITERIA.md
✓

Automated health checks

Every agent runs a real ACP initialize handshake once a week. A failure opens an issue automatically.

✓ health-checked

Versions stay current

Twice a day a job pulls the latest releases from npm, PyPI and GitHub Releases and commits the bumps on its own.

03 / how it works

A repo, a few scripts, no dashboard.

Each agent is a small YAML entry checked against CRITERIA.md. Scheduled GitHub Actions verify the ACP handshake, refresh versions from upstream package registries, and rebuild registry.json — the same file this page is reading right now.

curated-acp-agents/ ├─ agents/ one entry per agent ├─ scripts/ build · check · bump ├─ .github/workflows/ schedules ├─ CRITERIA.md inclusion rules └─ registry.json generated
04 / using the registry

Drop-in replacement for the official source

Every agent entry follows the official registry schema exactly, so any ACP client that reads a registry URL can point at this one instead. A top-level curation object adds our tier, status and health metadata — clients can ignore it.
